title: Identifier namespace and semantic role can disagree

scenario.observed_change: A consumer validates an identifier prefix and a component role independently but does not require those two identity representations to agree, allowing an artifact-prefixed component to be labeled and rendered as a capability.
mutable_state: consumer grouping and explanation derived from the role
authority_boundaries: canonical identifier namespace versus semantic role metadata
syntactic validation versus cross-field identity consistency
operation_model: provide a component whose identifier has a valid artifact namespace
assign a separately valid capability role
consumer exposes the component under the wrong semantic role

required_invariants.requirement: Identity mappings that jointly establish semantic meaning must cover materially reachable cross-field inconsistency, not only independent field syntax.

must_investigate: whether identifier namespace and role jointly encode the same semantic identity
whether cross-field mismatch is rejected before consumer grouping or explanation
must_identify: independent validation of both fields does not establish their required consistency
must_not_claim: valid component identity solely because the namespace and role are each individually allowed
correct consumer classification when the two semantic identity fields can disagree

provenance.note: Codex identified that a valid component ID prefix and a separately valid role could disagree, causing the Site consumer to render the component under the wrong semantic role.
